S1_incident_reporting.quote: Manufacturers shall report to the relevant regulator any thermal incident involving overheating, smoke, fire, injury, property damage, or emergency shut-down, within 24 hours of becoming aware of it, with a fuller initial investigation report within 10 calendar days. Manufacturers shall promptly notify affected customers when an incident indicates a safety risk or requires inspection, changed use, or corrective action, and in all cases within 5 calendar days of determining that such action is warranted. Suspected serious or imminent risks require immediate regulator and customer notification. Reporting obligations apply even when cause is uncertain.

S2_thermal_testing.quote: Each model shall undergo a sustained-heat test at 55 °C using a regulator-approved protocol and a statistically adequate sample. A model with a failure rate above 5% shall trigger regulator notification, a corrective-action plan and retesting within 12 months. Until it meets the limit, the regulator may require risk controls, sales restrictions or other proportionate measures; exceedance does not by itself require automatic permanent market exclusion.

S3_remote_shutoff.quote: All new units manufactured 18 months or more after this standard takes effect shall support remote emergency shut-off. For units already installed when the standard takes effect, manufacturers shall complete a technically feasible retrofit within 6 years; where retrofit is infeasible, they shall notify affected customers and the regulator, provide an alternative risk-control plan, and implement it promptly.

S4_fire_suppression.quote: All new units manufactured 36 months or more after this standard takes effect shall include built-in fire suppression meeting a regulator-approved performance and reliability protocol. Regulators may approve equivalent protective designs where they provide comparable fire-risk reduction.

S5_customer_disclosure.quote: A mandatory recall is triggered when a model’s annual thermal-incident rate exceeds 8 incidents per 100,000 units of that model installed during the year. Manufacturers shall promptly notify affected customers of material newly identified safety risks and provide updates on corrective actions.

document.section_notes: S1 is strong (24h reporting, immediate serious notice). S2 keeps 55°C/5% but allows open-ended sales with corrective action, so it is weakened. S3 sets new-unit shut-off at 18 months (weakened) but retrofit at 6 years (acceptable). S4 and S5 are acceptable: 36-month suppression with equivalent designs, and mandatory 8/100k recall without serious-injury clause.
